strengths: The paper addresses a meaningful problem: jointly choosing intervention variables and contextual observations. The introductory counterexample correctly demonstrates that standard CaBO and a fixed-scope CoBO policy can have strictly worse attainable rewards.
Combining established POMPS pruning with contextual Bayesian optimization provides a practical approach to continuous-variable problems beyond existing discrete mixed-policy methods.

Experiments use 110 seeds, 700 iterations, and uncertainty intervals. Including configurations where baselines can attain the optimum usefully exposes the overhead of scope selection, including a case where CoBO performs better.
weaknesses: The central UCB justification is incomplete. Each arm's reward distribution changes as its associated HEBO policy learns; stationarity at optimality does not justify stationary-bandit UCB during this learning process. No analysis establishes convergence of the coupled optimizers. Decreasing average regret over 700 iterations supports finite-horizon improvement, but does not establish asymptotic sublinear regret or the conclusion's claim of always reaching the optimum.

Support for general mixed policy scopes is underspecified. Definitions 3.1–3.2 permit different conditioning sets for different interventions, potentially requiring sequential decisions. Sections 4.1–4.2 instead describe joint optimization over X(S) given C(S), without explaining how individual information constraints and intervention-dependent context availability are enforced. The experiments do not exercise this difficulty.

The algorithm primarily combines existing POMPS theory, HEBO, and standard UCB, but the evaluation does not isolate the contribution of this combination. There are no controlled comparisons against alternative scope selectors using the same scopes and underlying optimizer. In particular, the PSA experiments have only one POMPS, so their improvements cannot demonstrate an advantage from UCB scope selection.

Evaluation breadth is insufficient for the efficiency and generality claims. All benchmarks are synthetic, and CoCa-BO considers only one or two candidate POMPSes. Appendix C mainly adds redundant variables; it does not test learning with many competing scopes or report scope-enumeration and optimization runtime.

The benchmark equations contain consequential inconsistencies. Appendix A.2 omits Cancer from the PSA structural equation, although the subsequent substitution and claimed sum-of-squares optimum require that term. Appendix C specifies C4 as depending on itself, contradicting the acyclic model. These may be transcription errors, but the experiments and analytic optima cannot be reproduced as written.

Implementation details are incomplete: the manuscript claims to share code but provides no repository link, and does not adequately specify the UCB exploration setting, initialization, baseline configurations, or several optimization domains. Section 5 also defines regret as observed reward minus optimal expected reward despite the maximization formulation and positive plotted regrets, leaving the reported metric's convention unclear.
